layers.description: Standalone Go binaries that boot the polyglot system — the server (HTTP/ConnectRPC/WebSocket), the probe (connectivity diagnostics), and the seed (dev data population).

layers.description: Orchestration of single use cases (network operations, business workflows, hotspot) that depend only on domain types and port interfaces — never on adapters or drivers.

layers.name: Port Contracts
layers.description: Go interfaces defining the contracts adapters and drivers must implement — device drivers, repositories, credential vault, audit writer, LLM provider, streaming, WhatsApp gateway, and caches.

layers.name: Adapter Layer
layers.description: Concrete implementations of the port contracts talking to external systems — ConnectRPC/HTTP handlers, MCP tools, WebSocket streaming, Postgres repositories, JWT/Casbin auth, LLM providers, Redis cache, and the credential vault.

layers.description: Vendor-specific network device drivers (Mikrotik, Cisco, generic SSH/Telnet via scrapligo, OLT vendors) plus the driver registry and YAML platform definitions.

layers.description: SQL migrations and the database tables they create (devices, bots, customers, subscriptions, invoices).

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what polyglot is: a NetOps + ISP management backend exposing MCP, REST, and WebSocket/SSE for multi-vendor network automation. Then check go.mod to see the stack — Gin, GORM, ConnectRPC, whatsmeow, scrapligo, go-routeros.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: cmd/server/main.go boots the server: it loads configuration, connects Postgres/Redis, wires the driver registry, and starts the Gin HTTP router, ConnectRPC services, and WebSocket streaming.

tour.title: Composition Root & Configuration
tour.description: internal/app/app.go is the dependency-injection hub wiring every adapter and use case together. internal/config/config.go loads runtime settings from the environment (documented in .env.example).

tour.title: Port Contracts
tour.description: The port layer defines the interfaces everything else depends on — DeviceDriver (execute/classify/translate), repositories, credential vault, LLM provider, audit writer, and streaming drivers. Adapters and drivers implement these.

tour.title: Domain Model
tour.description: internal/domain holds pure business entities and rules — device, command, session, customer, subscription, plan, billing. command.Command and its policy define what can be executed and what needs approval.

tour.title: Use Cases
tour.description: internal/usecase orchestrates single operations by calling ports — ExecuteCommand validates and runs a command through the driver, StreamOutput pipes live device output. Use cases never touch vendors directly.

tour.title: Device Drivers
tour.description: internal/driver contains one folder per vendor. Mikrotik speaks the RouterOS API via go-routeros; genericssh/generictelnet share a scrapligo engine driven by YAML platform definitions. Commands are classified destructive vs read-only per vendor.

tour.title: Driver Registry
tour.description: internal/registry selects and caches the right driver per device based on vendor and driver type, handing out ready-to-use connections.

tour.title: Adapters — API Surface
tour.description: Handlers in adapter/connect expose ConnectRPC services, adapter/mcp exposes MCP tools for LLM agents (get_device_status, run_command, push_config), and adapter/ws streams device output over WebSocket. The proto files in api/proto define the wire contracts.

tour.title: Adapters — Persistence, Auth, AI
tour.description: Postgres repositories implement the storage ports with GORM; Casbin + JWT enforce RBAC; LLM adapters (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Groq) back the assistant; Redis caches; the vault keeps device credentials encrypted.

tour.title: Data Layer
tour.description: Migrations create the schema — devices, bots, customers, and more. The devices table shows the columns the device model maps onto.

tour.title: Deployment & CI
tour.description: deployments/docker/Dockerfile builds the server image; docker-compose orchestrates server, Postgres, Redis, and WhatsApp services; the GitHub Actions workflow runs lint and tests.

tour.title: Architecture Docs
tour.description: Finish with Polyglot-Architecture.md and the ADRs in docs/adr to understand the why behind the design — why Gin, why driver interfaces without sessions, dual streaming connections, and scrapligo as the generic CLI engine.
